reasons: This is not a duplicate, and it deserves compute. I checked run_flow_atlas.py. Its day types are weekdays, gotobi, month-start and month-end ordinals, and US, Japan and England holidays. There is no calendar-month condition, so the month-of-year cut lies outside the atlas's search space. The cycle 4 ruling on gold_autumn_physical_demand applies here: the atlas Bonferroni bar (design t >= 3.7) covers re-slices of that space, so it does not bind; the programme pass bar (design t >= 2) does. The participant is dated and obligated and trades in Tokyo hours, the only kind of flow that has survived in this store. The pre-registration also carries a same-window control, gotobi separation, month-window clustering and a cross replication. The closest priors are already measured. In patterns_usdjpy, the fix-short to 06:00 UTC made +0.056 R (t 2.5) in design and -0.004 R in check on all days, and +0.022 / -0.048 R on non-gotobi days. So the plain Tokyo-session short is a cost-level effect that faded after 2017. Only the fiscal excess over the control can carry this test.

Calendar and cost counts on USDJPY M15, design 2010-2017. I counted dates, spreads and ATR only; no returns were computed. Every hypothesis slot is tradeable: ye_short mar n10 80/80, mar_sep n10 160/160, ctrl n10 471/480; ny_long mar n10 80/80, ctrl n10 466/479 (the gaps are the January 2010 ATR warm-up). The gotobi share is balanced between hypothesis and control: ye_short n10 30.0% vs 31.0%, ny_long n10 22.5% vs 23.2%. Gotobi therefore cancels in the rule-2 difference, and rule 3 tests it separately. The median ATR20 at entry is 87 pips, so the 0.25 x ATR stop is about 22 pips, not the 17 pips the rationale assumes. The mean fill spread is 0.68 pips at 00:00 UTC and 0.63 pips at 06:00 UTC. The round trip is about 1.06 pips of spread and slippage plus about 0.75 pip of commission, about 1.8 pips. That is about 0.08 R at sl 0.25 and 0.04 R at sl 0.5. On the crosses at sl 0.25 it is about 0.07 R for EURJPY (ATR 142 pips, fill spread 1.2-1.3), 0.10 R for AUDJPY (ATR 111, 1.5-1.6) and 0.08 R for GBPJPY (ATR 174, 2.1-2.4). A net +0.10 R therefore needs about +0.18 R gross, about 4 pips per Tokyo session, and the 1.5x hard gate removes another 0.04 R.

The ny_long control is contaminated in two ways. (a) It keeps January and July, the calendar-year and half-year starts. New-period allocations are made then: January Toshin launches and, from 2014, NISA flows. That is the mechanism under test. The proposal itself drops June and December from the month-end control for the same reason, but it keeps their month-start counterparts. (b) Tokyo is closed on 20.0% (n5) and 13.3% (n10) of the original ny_long control dates in design, and on 21.7% and 15.3% in check. The closures are 1-3 January, Golden Week (3-5 May), 3 November, 11 February and Coming-of-Age Day. The April and April+October cells have 0-5%. A control diluted with no-flow days pulls the control toward zero and biases the rule-2 difference toward the hypothesis. Months {2, 6, 8, 11, 12} have a 3.5-3.8% holiday share in design (3.3-5.0% in check), with 200 (n5) and 400 (n10) design slots. The ye_short control {1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 11} is fine as it stands. Its holiday share (0.4-2.5%) is lower than in the March cells (8.8%, the Vernal Equinox) and the March+September cells (11.9%), so any bias works against the hypothesis.

Raw-sign gates in check and the holdout would test USDJPY drift as much as the fiscal flow. In trending years the Tokyo-session share of USDJPY's drift is about 1.5-2 pips per session (2013 was +22% on the year, 2022 +14%). At the 0.25 stop that is 0.05-0.08 R, the same size as the hypothesised effect. ny_long is long USDJPY through the 2021-2023 rally in check, and ye_short is short against it. A raw 'check avg R > 0' gate therefore favours ny_long whether or not an April flow exists. The control difference cancels drift. It should decide in check and in the holdout as well as in design, as the cycle 4 review required for the gold seasonal (window minus rest in check and holdout).

The kill rules and the pipeline do not line up, in three places. (a) Rule 1 picks one best cell across both legs, but rule 7 says the legs are separate claims, so the losing leg is never judged on its own. (b) Rule 1 requires 80 trades, which excludes the mar n5 cells (40 trades). The pipeline's stage B/C selection admits them (min_design_n is 30). The cell the pipeline validates on USDJPY can therefore differ from the rule-1 cell. Under month-window clustering, mar n5 and mar n10 share the same 8 clusters, so the 80-trade floor protects nothing the clustered t does not already protect. (c) With both legs in the B/C spec grid, stage B can pick different legs on different markets, and the walk-forward (4-year train, 1-year test, re-optimised by t) can switch legs from year to year. The pooled check and walk-forward hard gates would then test a mix of two claims with opposite signs on different dates.

Rule 4b (drop the best two month-windows) is too blunt for the 8-window March cells. Suppose the effect is real at +0.10 R and month-window means have an sd of about 0.22 R (0.7 R / sqrt(10)). The expected top two of 8 such windows sit about +1.4 and +0.85 sd above the mean. Dropping them leaves an expected mean of about +0.02 R, so the rule kills a true effect about half the time. Dropping only the single best window already catches the one-episode case, such as a March 2011 or March 2020 outlier. For the 16-window March+September cells, dropping two is reasonable.

Power and value are low. There are 8 independent Marches in design (16 with September). At the registered +0.10 R and t 1.2-1.5, the chance of reaching the pass bar (design t >= 2) is about 25% even if the effect is real, and rules 1-6 together will kill a real effect more often than not. If it does pass, 10-20 trades a year at about +0.1 R adds +1-2 R a year. Also, 30% of ye_short dates are gotobi days, when the basket's gotobi leg is already short USDJPY, so that part stacks risk rather than diversifying it. The rationale's claim that month-end Tokyo flows are larger than ordinary gotobi flows is not supported: +0.176 R (t 1.72, 94 trades) against +0.144 R for all gotobi days is a gap well inside noise. Approval rests on cheap compute and on closing the last unscanned calendar dimension, as the Director's note intends, not on an expected tradeable edge.
reviews.revisions: 1) Control months by leg. 'ctrl' means H_short = {1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 11} for ye_short (unchanged) and H_long = {2, 6, 8, 11, 12} for ny_long. This drops the January and July new-period starts and the Golden Week month, and adds the ordinary non-quarter month-starts of June and December. The grid stays at 24 cells. Expected ny_long ctrl slots: design about 200 (n5) and 400 (n10); check 150 and 300. 2) Kill rules apply per leg. Rule 1 for each leg: the eligible cells are that leg's 8 hypothesis cells (months in {mar, mar_sep}). Set the minimum to 40 design trades (min_trades_design_per_market = 40). The chosen cell is the one with the highest trade-level design t, the same ranking the pipeline uses. It must have design avg R > 0, trade-level t >= 1 and month-window-clustered t >= 1. Rules 2-6 then use that leg's chosen cell and its matching ctrl cell (same leg, n_days and sl_atr). 3) Control difference in check and holdout. Add to rule 2: kill if check avg R(chosen) - check avg R(matching ctrl cell) <= 0. The stage A backtests span design and check, so read all 24 stage A rows from the trials table (stage 'A'); the report keeps only the top 15. If the leg is promoted, the locked run also runs the matching ctrl cell on the holdout years (same touch, counted). A holdout where chosen minus ctrl <= 0 is a fail even if the raw holdout avg R > 0. 4) Rule 4b: drop the best ceil(W/8) design month-windows, where W is the number of month-windows in the cell (1 for mar cells, 2 for mar_sep cells). Design avg R must stay > 0. Rule 4a (at least half the design years positive) stays. 5) Spec grids. stage_a = {market: USDJPY, grid: the full 24 cells}. The spec grid for stages B and C, the walk-forward and any holdout holds one leg only: {leg: [ye_short], months: [mar, mar_sep], n_days: [5, 10], sl_atr: [0.25, 0.5]} (8 cells). ye_short is the primary claim because its participants face a balance-sheet deadline. If ye_short fails rules 1-5 at stage A but the automatic floor lets the pipeline continue (an ny_long or ctrl cell cleared t >= 1), ignore its B/C output and scrap ye_short under rule 1. If ny_long passes rules 1-5 at stage A, it gets its own counted B/C run with leg [ny_long] in the same 8-cell shape. Read rule 6 at the leg's rule-1 cell on each cross from the stage B trials table. Pool the three crosses date-clustered: average the same-date R across crosses, then compute t over dates. 6) Expectations. Replace the cost line with: USDJPY stop about 22 pips at sl 0.25 (median design ATR20 87 pips); round trip about 1.8 pips, about 0.08 R at sl 0.25 and 0.04 R at sl 0.5; crosses 0.07-0.10 R at sl 0.25; +0.10 R net needs about +0.18 R gross, about 4 pips per Tokyo session. Add: P(design t >= 2 | effect real at +0.10 R) is about 25%; a positive below the bar is recorded as below the bar and not promoted. Delete the claim that the month-end-only gotobi variant shows larger month-end flows. 7) Exit guard. Also skip the date if m.ts[xi] is more than 60 minutes after d 06:00 UTC, so a data gap cannot stretch the hold into the next session. My count found no such date in design, so this changes nothing in practice. 8) Diagnostics, reported and not gating: for each leg's chosen cell, avg R and count on (a) Japanese public holidays inside the window (Vernal Equinox in late March, the September holidays, Sports Day; 8.8% of ye_short mar n10 dates and 11.9% of mar_sep n10 dates) and (b) Good Friday and Easter Monday dates (3 of 80 ye_short mar n10 dates, 8 of 80 ny_long mar n10 dates); plus a per-year table of chosen minus ctrl in design and check.
reviews.notes_for_builder: Contract details. (1) dates = np.unique(F.utc_dates(m)), keep F.weekday(dates) < 5 and dates >= np.datetime64(p['start']). month = (dates.astype('datetime64[M]').astype(np.int64) % 12) + 1. k = F.kth_last_weekday(dates) and rank = np.busday_count(dates.astype('datetime64[M]').astype('datetime64[D]'), dates). Both are calendar-based, so a missing data day does not shift them. ye_short selects 0 <= k < n_days; ny_long selects rank < n_days. (2) Month sets come from a per-leg mapping: {'mar': ({3}, {4}), 'mar_sep': ({3, 9}, {4, 10}), 'ctrl': ({1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 11}, {2, 6, 8, 11, 12})}. The first set is for ye_short, the second for ny_long. Raise on an unknown leg or months value. (3) eh, em = F.parse_hhmm(p['entry_utc']) and xh, xm = F.parse_hhmm(p['exit_utc']). ei = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, sel_dates, eh, em) and xi = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, sel_dates, xh, xm). Skip the date if ei < 1, ei >= m.n, xi >= m.n, xi <= ei, m.ts[ei] - (d + entry time) > p['max_delay_min'] minutes, or m.ts[xi] - (d + exit time) > 60 minutes. sig = ei - 1. Set entry_short[sig] (ye_short) or entry_long[sig] (ny_long), entry_type 0, valid_bars 1, tp_dist NaN, max_bars 0. The exit flag goes on xi - 1 (exit_short or exit_long), which is >= ei because xi > ei. (4) daily = F.daily_bars(m); atr = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, p['atr_n'])). Skip if atr[ei] is not finite or <= 0. sl_dist[sig] = p['sl_atr'] * atr[ei]. Read atr at ei, not sig: ei's trading day starts at 17:00 NY the previous evening, so the value is known before entry. (5) PARAMS must contain every key: leg, months, n_days, sl_atr, entry_utc, exit_utc, max_delay_min, atr_n, start. Read every key from p; no holiday table and no randomness. A Python loop over selected dates is fine. (6) Expected counts for the checker, USDJPY design years: ye_short mar n10 = 80, mar_sep n10 = 160, ctrl n10 = 471 (480 slots less the ATR warm-up); ny_long mar n10 = 80, mar_sep n10 = 160, ctrl n10 about 395-400 with the revised months. The n5 cells are half of these. A count far from these numbers means the date selection is wrong.
